requires.hardware: Python 3.11+ and standard library for the host reference; backend hardware is an engine choice; C++20 and Core's files library (crit::core) for native gather
requires.model: Expert weights described as immutable encoded file regions; no fixed tensor shape or storage device
requires.workload: Demand/read-ahead file materialization with bounded staging and separate read/upload lifetimes

contract.input: ExpertRegion records, immutable file and executor/upload hooks
contract.output: Encoded expert bytes or Materialization(owner, encoded_source, readiness); native gather returns owned bytes in region order and advice/worker counters
contract.ownership: Source owns pending reads and retains bytes/upload services after ambiguous enqueue. Successful Materialization retains both copy endpoints/readiness. Upload service retains partial destinations; read quiescence does not prove upload quiescence. Native gathers retain their immutable mapping, borrowed request descriptors and private output through every joined task; POSIX callers prevent file mutation/truncation.
contract.failure: Reject malformed/changed extents, missing experts and closed-source reads. Failed-upload staging survives until explicit physical upload-quiescence proof. Native mapping validates byte/region/worker caps and drains launched tasks; mapping does not verify checksums or convert OS mapping faults into C++ exceptions.
contract.core_boundary: The native file handle, read-only mapping, change detection and read-ahead hint are Core's ReadOnlyFile; this entry adds the sparse coalesced gather. Use core-owned upload buffers/streams; expert representation and prefetch selection remain consumer policy.

dependencies: C++20 threads/futures and Core's files library (crit::core)

validation.host: Host fixtures and worked example cover checked file reads, pending reuse, read failure and failed-upload retention/recovery
validation.native: Windows and Linux fixtures check mapped page boundaries, duplicates, coalescing, sequential/parallel equivalence, empty files, bounds, cancellation and retry; no storage-throughput or GPU-upload qualification
validation.performance: Unmeasured for a native engine; host fixture success is not a speed claim
